Guns, explosions, and monster trucks. Is this what's considered "entertainment"? Thrown into a post-apocalyptic world, we are shown dynamics between governor and governed that are simply laughable, as if hoarding all the water from the population wouldn't cause an immediate uprising and lead to a proto-communist society. Scenes made purely to get a confused or indignant reaction from the spectator, making each ridiculous moment appear even more senseless than the prior. Despite having really gorgeous cinematography and color grading, everything else is as close to horrible as possible. Editing, VFX, and acting (by some charactes), are all lackluster, something that is amplified by the fact that the film has no real story to tell. I believe this is even more unengaging than Maze Runner 2 — my first one star review on Letterboxd— which at least had a malformed concept of a plot going on from the first movie of the saga, unlike what I've just watched. I don't enjoy these post-apocalyptic, survival action stories, with the sole exceptions being both The Last of Us games (so far), but I went into this film without any expectations whatsoever; so being met with with the most mindless, generic, action (sub)plot I've seen made me irritated from the start. I genuinely cannot understand how this can be so famous and well received as it is, do the people really live for the idea of turning off their brains for two hours and accepting the most wacky shit the director and writer could think of after snorting moldy chalk? Infuriating. Fuck this!

Reminds me a lot of Star Wars Episode 1 in the way the film is focused on self-important lore and world-building above all else, turning its back on the fizzy melodramatic fun of the original works. None of the characters are engaging, little of the action is exciting, everything is so transparently in service of delivering lame jargon and iconography, which all has a smug 1960s hippie vibe to it that I find totally insufferable. The extent to which it is impossible to give a shit about Max or Furiosa is remarkable, they're not cool, charming, funny, self-reflective or in possession of any other potentially humanising traits, just relentless grim stoicism. Perhaps if the film were not saddled with one of Tom Hardy's most moronically misjudged performances and Max had some kind of charisma, like Mel Gibson achieved without sacrificing intensity, the viewer would have had some kind of way in to the film on an emotional level, shame no one reigned him in. Also remarkable is how unexpectedly slow it is, both dialogue and action scenes dragging terribly - take the scene where Max first holds Furiosa and the wives at gunpoint, it goes on so long with so little of any significance happening that it starts to become awkward, the characters just standing and looking at eachother. This absolutely feels like it was directed by a 70 year old and edited by someone with no prior action film experience. Of course there's a lot of spectacle, but you mainly consume it with a dispassionate appreciation of the scale and detail of the production design and the work that must have gone into realising it, rarely approaching the edge of your seat. Miller just isn't a good enough action director to cope with the scale he's aiming for here - within the huge road-fleets there's no real sense of where the active characters are in relation to eachother, of who is in which samey vehicle or where the danger will be coming from, so the feeling that the baddies are just popping into existence to fulfil a quota for action within an artificial entertainment becomes too nagging. Would also help if this hadn't aimed for a PG-13 rating, more graphic violence would at least provoke a visceral reaction to what's happening on screen that you don't get when the film is constantly shying away from the reality of people getting shot in the head or blown up or crushed by huge trucks. A lot of people seem to be very passionate fans of Fury Road and yet the follow-up was a huge financial flop, so why didn't they turn up for it in droves? I think the reality is that it's easy to make this film sound conceptually cool on paper, but on a more nuts-and-bolts level it is let down by weak direction - the idea of the film is better than the reality.

A ver, primero que nada: no llegué a terminar la película. Pero si soy completamente sincera, los primeros 40 minutos fueron suficientes. Para muestra, basta un botón. Igual voy a ser buena y darle una oportunidad y terminarla, porque sé que tiene una cantidad absurda de críticas positivas y probablemente haya algo que todavía no estoy viendo. Pero si tengo que sacar una primera conclusión es que me está resultando muy difícil tomarme en serio lo que estoy viendo. No porque la propuesta sea exagerada (esa es parte de su identidad) sino porque muchas de las situaciones me resultan poco verosímiles incluso dentro de la lógica que plantea la propia historia. Lo que más me llama la atención es que se nota que tiene muchísimo presupuesto, pero pareciera que se olvidaron de ponerlo en el guion. Desde el principio me hice millones de preguntas sobre la lógica de esta peli: decisiones sin sentido, situaciones que parecen contradecir las propias reglas que plantea la película e inconsistencias de los personajes. Y creo que ese es mi principal problema: No logra hacerte entrar en su mundo. Es una distopía en la que casi no hay agua, el sol parece querer quemar a todo el mundo y solo lo mas importante para mostrar es como una sociedad decide resolver sus problemas manejando vehículos a toda velocidad por un desierto. Esta premisa puede ser completamente delirante, es justamente por eso q necesitás construir muy bien la trama y las reglas de ese universo para que el espectador diga “okay, esto está loco pero tiene sentido dentro de este mundo” y pueda empatizarrr. Además todo ocurre a una velocidad tan frenética y fría que lo hace todavía más difícil de procesar y así de apoco deja de impresionarte lo que ves. Todo está puesto al servicio de la acción, mientras que la trama y los personajes principales quedan bastante relegados. Y hablando de personajes, tampoco están tan buenos. El protagonista: tipo sensillo, fuerte, misterioso, sarcástico, antihéroe, con pasado trágico y prácticamente todas las características clásicas para que un hombre conecte. El villano es una cosa cochina no se que más decir. Y después están los personajes femeninos. Acá me costó mucho comprar el supuesto mensaje de empoderamiento. Tenemos un grupo de mujeres que son literalmente modelos, todas extremadamente atractivas, vestidas con muy poca ropa, ingenuas e indefensas. Incluso mantienen una actitud cariñosa con una persona que les hizo daño. Hay un personaje femenino que sí se presenta como fuerte y capaz, pero incluso no termina de despegarse de ciertos clichés. Visualmente la película es espectacular. Probablemente sea lo que más puedo rescatar hasta ahora. Tiene una estética muy original y extremadamente reconocible. Todo es exagerado y artificial, pero creo que justamente esa artificialidad es parte de su identidad. El mundo se siente quemado por el sol, los colores son súper contrastantes, los vehículos y personajes tienen diseños increíbles y cada plano parece pensado para ser visualmente muy impactante y llamativo. La música también acompaña muy bien toda esta locura. Si querés una película superficial, no tenés ganas de analizar demasiado la lógica de lo que estás viendo, querés acción prácticamente constante, paisajes increíbles, personajes visualmente muy llamativos y poco interés por el lore o la construcción del mundo, probablemente esta sea tu película. Pero bueno, en cuanto a la trama, se podría haber hecho y aprovechado muchísimo más (y sin hacer falta sacrificar acción) Hacer una película de 2 horas que básicamente trata sobre vehículos peleando en un desierto es una idea muy arriesgada. Para que funcione, hay que saber atrapar al espectador y hacer que le importe lo que está pasando no solo entretenerlo con explosiones y colores. Igual, voy a terminarla. Capaz dentro de una hora vuelvo acá a borrar absolutamente todo esto. Ojalá...

Mad Max Fury Road (2015) von George Miller, erzählt von einer Verfolgungsjagd durch eine postapokalyptische Welt. Der Film hat in erster Linie sehr starke Actionszenen zu bieten, welche gehäuft auftreten und atemberaubend sind. Die inszenierte Welt weckt aber kaum mein Interesse. Sie wirkt auf mich überinszeniert und wenig kohärent. Diese Überinszenierung erzeugt bei mir eher Distanz als Faszination. Zudem finde ich abgesehen von Furiosa und Nux kaum einen Charakter interessant. Besonders die Antagonisten wirken eher wie groteske Symbole, die sehr einprägsam sind, aber für mich keine interessanten Figuren darstellen. Auch Max weckt kein besonderes Interesse bei mir. Oft sieht man Rückblicke, welche bei mir eher unbeantwortete Fragen aufwerfen als Interesse am Charakter. Dass die Charakterentwicklung auch über die Action geschieht, ist mir bewusst, dennoch kann ich mich damit nicht anfreunden. Der Film hat eine sehr simple Handlung, die aus einer Verfolgung besteht, was ich auch als eine der Stärken sehe. Es wird nicht versucht krampfhaft etwas Komplexes erzählen. Dass Start und Endpunkt derselbe sind, ist nett inszeniert gibt dem Film meiner Meinung nach aber auch keine besondere Tiefe.

A film with a detailed world and impressive sets but just another standard non stop action movie. This is my first Mad Max film simply because I haven't been very interested in the series. I do however play games in my free time and after playing Mad Max on the Xbox I thought maybe I should give some of the films a go. Considering Fury road had some extremely positive reviews and starred Tom Hardy I had high hopes. I would have probably been better to assume the worst and be pleasantly surprised though. While it has some things going for it, overall I found it just another average action movie. The set design, world building, costume and sets are impressively immersive and the creators have done an impressive job creating a genuinely unique and believable world. The desert landscapes look incredible and are paired with some excellent cinematography that really brings the world to life. The costume design really brings the characters to life and when paired within the immersive environment it genuinely feels like the world has its own culture and history. Another great element is that it does actually feel like a non stop action film. I personally found the endless action a bit monotonous but if you are a fan of action films this is certainly something you will enjoy. Once the characters hit the fury road, the violence and intensity just keeps hammering away right until the bitter end. I wouldn't say I didn't enjoy the film at all, but for me the endless action didn't allow for any character or story development at all and at times it felt completely exhausting personally. It's just not enough for me to consider it a great film, it is however action paced, immersive and fun. It's also visually stunning and has some incredible stunts and vehicle sequences that offer a unique experience. Mad max is a simple and streamlined action film that's genuinely fun and is complete non stop action. While it has an excellent and immersive world I did find the action became a bit exhausting and did at times wish they spent more time offering viewers any sort of depth or character development. A genuine action film but nothing you haven't seen before from the genre. 6 / 10 Dave Kaye (Bilbo Bagsy) 13/09/2026

Well folks, here's a smidgen of controversy for you.....I wasn't blown away by Fury Road! I mean it's a great chase movie, it has insane stunts, amazing vehicles, machine gun editing, it's playful with film speed, it features the legend that is Hugh Keays-Byrne, Toecutter from the very first movie, as Immortan Joe in his final film role, fun bad guys, Tom and Charlize snarling at each other, and and and...so much is going on!! And I'm exhausted. I just can't see this being the best Mad Max film as some do. It's all a matter of personal taste I guess. And my personal taste, also controversially, still rates the OG Mad Max as the one that means the most to me. I watched it on first release in London with my old man, and it was of course unlike anything I'd seen before. So bleak, such an unfamiliar backdrop, as I'd basically only seen Hollywood or old British movies up to then, such a scary film. And no familiar actors to feel safe with. I also have a soft spot for number 2, the Road Warrior, a great follow up. And like many I was deeply disappointed with Thunder Dome. Fury Road is a definite improvement over that last entry, absolutely no doubt. But call me an old reactionary or simply a fuddy-duddy, I need something more than an extended chase to wow me, however frenetic or visually resplendent. I appreciate great stunts, but I miss the days when CGI wasn't a thing, however much it 'enhances' the action. And lastly, as much as I usually love Tom Hardy he's no Mel Gibson, he's not the Max I grew up with, he's completely different, and I'd have less problem if his character had not been named Max. For most of the running time he wasn't even the main character, and Furiosa was so much more dynamic. I'll stop there. I did honestly enjoy Fury Road, but I found it good rather than great.

Putting this on my 75” TV was such a blast, honestly. An excellent piece and a monumental achievement of 21st-century cinema, delivering a magical experience that exquisitely balances utterly chaotic yet really aesthetic action with surprisingly subtle, but deeply powerful, emotion. George Miller deserves every bit of praise for what he built here, simply immaculate. Beyond Miller’s direction, the sheer amount of care put into the cinematography, score, editing, production design, and both the practical and visual effects is peak filmmaking. Story-wise might not seem like much on the surface, but it proves incredibly effective through its straightforward premise, engaging structure, and hidden depth. Genuinely feels like a nearly two-hour chase pumped full of adrenaline, yet Miller knows exactly when to slow things down, add new layers, and reinvent the action so it never becomes stale. Miller also does an incredible job with the organic world-building, making us care about these characters while establishing a surprisingly strong thematic core. Charlize Theron and Tom Hardy shouldn’t be overlooked either; both bring so much subtlety and nuance to their performances, grounding this wonderfully quirky world and turning their respective versions of Furiosa and Max into memorable roles. And the sheer awesomeness of this movie extends to details, such as having an entire band literally playing music in the middle of all the chaos, which we we found absolutely freaking incredible lol. Simply put, this is a film that’s almost unimpeachable on a technical level, that narratively one could argue that it falls a little behind, and obviously it isn’t on the same level there, but even then, it manages to find something genuinely powerful within all the chaos.
